title: Padded gap eras are indistinguishable from real rows: era_row/era_advance_validate accept an empty Era_Row as a valid advance target
detail: An eras.json with era 1 and era 3 (no era 2) loads clean: the padded empty row passes era_row and the FSM validates/fires an advance into an era with an empty roster and no demand binding — the exact drift fail-fast exists to reject.
recommended_fix: Reject non-contiguous era tables at load (require every era 1..max present), or check the row is populated (id != "") in era_row/era_advance_validate.

title: Load comment claims unique era ids but no uniqueness check exists
evidence:
// (strict int, 1..64, unique — the same domain as the demand rows),
	// `id`/`display_name` (non-empty, unique ids), `packet_types` (the ACTIVE
detail: The duplicate guard only covers the era number (`seen[era-1]`); two rows with the same `id` load clean despite the documented uniqueness invariant. Either enforce or stop claiming it.
recommended_fix: Add an id-uniqueness pass over parsed rows (linear, map-free per ODN-10) or delete "unique ids" from the contract comment.

title: log_write puts a defaulted parameter before a non-defaulted one — suspicious Odin signature that contradicts the claimed green build
evidence: log_write :: proc(state: ^Run_State, scratch := context.temp_allocator, header_era: u8) -> []u8 {
detail: A defaulted parameter (`scratch`) precedes a mandatory one (`header_era`); Odin requires default parameters to trail, so this either fails to compile (contradicting the diff's own 'ci-local 10/10, app build' claims) or silently reorders call semantics.
recommended_fix: Make the signature `log_write :: proc(state: ^Run_State, header_era: u8, scratch := context.temp_allocator)` and update the five call sites accordingly.

title: Demo lowering validates an advance only against the START era, not prior advances — duplicate/non-forward chains bless a replay_error log
detail: The comment vows 'never let a bad demo bless a poisoned log', yet two `advance 3` lines (or 3 then 4 then 3) pass lowering; at apply the second fails validation and latches replay_error in the blessed log — precisely the failure mode the check claims to prevent.
recommended_fix: Track a running expected era across sorted advances at lower time and reject any to_era not strictly forward of the previous target.

title: era_step takes cat but never uses it; comments claim it 'loads the new era's unlocks'
detail: The body touches only state; `cat` is dead. The step.odin seam comment says era_step 'loads the new era's unlocks' — nothing is loaded; the unlocks are pure catalog queries. The parameter and the comment both overclaim.
recommended_fix: Drop the cat parameter (update the step.odin call) or use it (e.g., assert era_row(cat, new_era)); fix the 'loads the unlocks' wording either way.

title: Demand-switch test hardcodes streaming's class index instead of resolving it
detail: `e.class == 1` assumes streaming is packet_types index 1; a reorder of packet_types.json flips the assertion to a false pass/fail. The same file resolves indices via class_index everywhere else.

title: Era domain is documented as both 1..6 and 1..64 within the same change
detail: The serializer comment justifies the u8 payload with a 1..6 era domain; the loader accepts 1..64. Both fit a u8, so this is only documentation drift today, but the 1..6 claim will be wrong the moment eras 4-6+ land.
recommended_fix: State the real bound (u8 payload covers the catalog's 1..64 domain) instead of the content-specific 1..6.

title: A missing demand_era key reports 'has no demand.json row' instead of 'missing field'
detail: A row that omits demand_era defaults to 0 and errors 'demand_era 0 has no demand.json row' — a misleading message for a missing field, now blessed by the test. Fail-fast ergonomics suffer for no reason.
recommended_fix: Distinguish absent-key from out-of-range (separate jint presence check) and emit 'demand_era is required' for the former.
